**Failed transaction?** Yes. The account was debited on 19 Nov 2026 but confirmation never reached the merchant's system and no order was created; the failure was not attributable to the customer. This fits "Card Not Present (CNP) (e-commerce): account debited but confirmation not received at merchant's system" (Sl. 2(c) of the Annex). The 18 Nov ₹1,860 purchase was successful and is excluded.

**Deadline:** Auto-reversal within T+5 days. T = 19 Nov. Counting five calendar days: 20, 21, 22, 23, 24 → outer limit **24 Nov 2026**.

**Late?** Yes. Reversal credited on 27 Nov, i.e., delay days beyond T+5 are 25, 26, 27 = **3 days**.

**Compensation:** ₹100 per day of delay × 3 = **₹300**, payable to the customer's account suo moto without any claim form, as per paragraphs 5 and Sl. 2(c).

**Action:** Credit ₹300 automatically; do not close the complaint on refund alone.

**Note on the ₹450 penal charge (RBI circular DoR.MCS.REC.28/01.01.001/2023-24, dated 18.08.2023)**

Para 3(vi) requires the quantum and reason for any penal charge to be clearly disclosed in the loan agreement, the applicable KFS/Most Important Terms & Conditions, and on the website under Interest Rates and Service Charges. Here, none of the three discloses the amount or the reason for this charge — a clear gap to be corrected before any further levy.

Para 3(vii) requires that reminders for non-compliance communicate the applicable penal charge, and that any levy be communicated with the reason. The 13 November reminder mentioned only "charges"; the 17 November debit notice gave the amount and reference but not the reason (the missing stock statement). Both fell short.

On refund: the circular sets disclosure, reasonableness (para 3(iv)) and communication requirements but does not itself provide that an undisclosed charge is automatically refundable. Whether ₹450 must be reversed depends on reasonableness and Board policy — facts not established here. Compliance gaps and the borrower's grievance should still be addressed.

**Liability कितनी?** यह तीसरे पक्ष का breach है जिसमें न बैंक की और न आपकी कमी है। परिपत्र के अनुसार zero liability तभी मिलती है जब बैंक के संदेश (2 नवंबर) मिलने के **3 कार्य-दिवस** के भीतर शिकायत हो। आपकी शाखा के कार्य-समय से गणना करने पर (2 को छोड़कर: 3, 4, 5 नवंबर) आपकी शिकायत 13 नवंबर को हुई, अर्थात् 7 कार्य-दिवस से भी बाद। ऐसी स्थिति में liability **बैंक की बोर्ड-अनुमोदित policy** से तय होगी — परिपत्र से कोई सटीक रुपया-राशि नहीं निकलती। इसलिए ₹14,200 में से कोई हिस्सा अभी तय नहीं किया जा सकता।

**Policy दिखाना ज़रूरी है?** हाँ — बैंक को यह policy वेबसाइट पर प्रदर्शित करनी होगी और ग्राहकों को व्यक्तिगत रूप से सूचित करना अनिवार्य है।

**सबूत कौन देगा?** ग्राहक की liability साबित करने का बोझ **बैंक पर** है।

कृपया बैंक से उसकी Board-approved policy की प्रति माँगें — देना उसकी जिम्मेदारी है।
